question.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions to the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-3 \\ 3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-7.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=-3$ and ${y}_{2}=2.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

- Next, we solve $Ux=y.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3 \\ 2{x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${x}_{2}=1$ and ${x}_{1}=-1.$ Therefore, 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{2}=(-1)\cdot 2=-2.$
